content.content:
## How the map reaches the writer

The clarity workflow's assessor and writer read the folder of their chunk. With adjustment 15 of `../../ADJUSTMENTS.md` applied (its two clauses in `record-clarity/assess.md` and `writer.md`, in `../tools.patch`), they read `scout.md` when it is there. They read nothing else of the map: no brief of the clarity workflow names `MAP.md`, `map.json` or a claims file. So the map reaches them only through `scout.md`, and only with adjustment 15.

After each scout, `map-lines.py` adds to the chunk's `scout.md`, for each entry of the chunk: the map's line, which gives its disposition (stays, rewritten in place, merged into F-n, split, with each part and the entry that it goes to, a defect's description to row N, not about the tree); the subjects of its claims, each with the entry that owns it; the claims to move out, by kind; its defects and their rows; today's checks; its groups of overlap; the parts that other entries send to it; and its block of the claims file, word for word, with each claim, its subject and its kind. Each other entry that it names is marked as in this chunk or not. The script writes nothing else, and a second call replaces its section, so a resumed run adds it once.

The map's lines are data. No brief of the clarity workflow tells the assessor or the writer to follow a disposition. The writer reads `references/record.md`, "What an entry is", which asks for one subject in each entry, a split where claims change apart, a claim moved to the entry that holds its subject, and a merge into the entry that owns the subject. The assessor's "reorganize" names a merge and a split.

What the clarity workflow can write, by its apply file (`record.py`'s header): new lines for several entries of the chunk, a new entry (`F-?1`), `merge F-n into F-m`, `move` and `remove`. So a split, a merge or a claim moved between two entries of one chunk can be written; the run of 2026-10-22 merged F-246 into F-259.

What it cannot do as it stands:

- **Move a claim to an entry outside the chunk.** The writer is given its chunk's entries. The checker, the second cold reader and the judge rule on those entries only, and the judge's `final.apply` copies only their blocks. A part that the map sends outside the chunk is kept where it is, or cut with no line that receives it. `map.json` lists 53 such parts across its chunks (`cross_chunk_parts`); a chunk's lines in `scout.md` name each of its own.
- **Rewrite an entry that the assessor keeps.** The writer, the checker and the judge get only the entries that the assessor marks reword or reorganize (`record-clarity.js`, its first stage). An entry that it keeps is not rewritten, even where the map sends claims to it or merges another entry into it.
- **Judge a move as a move.** The checker compares each new entry with that entry's old text and its sources. A claim moved from one entry to another reads as "says less" at the first and "adds a claim" at the second, unless the checker sees the move.
- **List where each claim went.** `proposals.md` gives the source of each sentence of a new text, and the apply file's note line the pointers that left an entry. No file lists, for each claim that left an entry, where it now stands.

## What it reuses from the clarity workflow, and what it leaves to the coordinator

It reuses the clarity workflow whole, unchanged: its script, its briefs, its seven stages for each chunk, its writer streams, its folder for each chunk, and its README's "After a chunk". The script starts it as a child run, as `record-landing.js` starts the orientation update: `workflow({ scriptPath: '.../record-clarity/record-clarity.js' }, { kind, out, stream, chunks })`, with `out` the batch folder's `chunks/`. The scouts write `scout.md` into the same chunk folder before the child run starts.

A child run shares its parent's two agents at once. So the chunks go side by side as several runs of this script, each with one child run, and not as several children of one run.

It leaves to the coordinator:

- the curator's go after each round of the pilot, and the page that he reads;
- every write to the record on `main`: each `final.apply`, the leave step's file and the sweep's file, applied with `record.py`, checked, committed and pushed;
- the shares of the chunks among runs, and `runs.json`;
- the review queue and the concepts list, from each chunk's `queue.md` and `concepts.md`;
- the decision on each held entry, and the size of the record after each chunk;
- unblinding the test.

No agent of this script writes the record. The claims and map workers commit and push their own files in `sorting/`, as their briefs of 2026-11-24 did.

## Where the briefs come from

**Taken word for word, but for the changes listed:**

- `briefs/scout.txt`: October's scouts' template of 2026-10-13, `../../evidence/october-briefs/03-scouts-template.md`. Two changes: an entry's number is now its `F-n` or `P-n`, where October's brief took its line number at a commit (the entries had no numbers yet); and the commit `715641924` is now `@BASE@`.
- `briefs/sweep.txt`: the brief of the scrape of 2026-10-22, "Scrape status out of the record", copied from the transcript (part `B/002`, line 10748, of the folder `fe616d40-a9c6-56d7-9da1-7168a172765d.until-2026-11-07T23-09.jsonl.parts/` under `/home/user/fortress-transcripts-blinded/projects/-home-user-fortress/`); its result was commit `3822898328`. Three changes: that day's two exceptions cut (F-112's source, and F-238 and F-223 repointed), the sentence on their check cut to "Fix every failure.", and its folder made `@OUT@`.
- `briefs/test-grader.txt`: the kit's `brief-grader.md` of 2026-10-13, with the four changes that `record-test/2026-11-24/README.md`, "What the kit's grader brief needs changed", gives. "The same twelve scenarios" is written "the same scenarios", so that the brief fits any set.
- The readers' brief is the kit's `brief-reader.md`, used in place, unchanged.
- `briefs/claims.txt`: the coordinator's brief of 2026-11-24, `../../evidence/sorting-map/brief-claims.md`. Four changes: "339 entries" cut; the chunks come in the launch message, not from that night's `chunks.json`; that night's scouts' files and list of stale claims are now `@CHECKS@`; its output folder is now `@SORT@`.
- `briefs/map.txt`: the coordinator's brief of 2026-11-24, saved word for word as `../../evidence/sorting-map/brief-map.md`. Changes: that night's counts ("339", "six workers", "twelve files") cut; its paths now `@SORT@`, `@CLAIMS@` and `@SCENARIOS@`; "Include F-63 if it fits a case, since the curator asked about it." now `@ASKED@`, filled from `asked`; "in the morning" cut.

October had no brief for the sorting of FACTS: its sections already stood by area, and the model of the sorting is the gap ledger's grouping of 2026-10-08 (`../../WORKFLOW-DIFF.md`, B1). So the two sorting briefs are tonight's.

**Kept in part:** `briefs/leave.txt`, from October's "Step 12: retire the old homes", `../../evidence/october-briefs/07b-step12-brief-as-edited.md`. Kept: the role line's form, the goal with the curator's words of 2026-10-13, "leaves now only where its rule already stands in that skill as it is today; otherwise it stays, and you list it with its home", the grep before each removal, the note that names the home, and the empty headings. Cut, as October's own: the outline of the coordinator skill that was its map of homes, the clauses marked "(moves to ...)", the rewrite of the record's header comments, the README and the protocol, INDEX and HELD. Changed:
  1. What leaves is `@LEAVE@`, limited to entries that are not about the project, by the curator's word of 2026-11-24 (`../../HIS-WORDS.md`, 5.3; `../../WORKFLOW-DIFF.md`, B8).
  2. October's worker applied its file on `main` and committed. Here it writes the file and checks it on a copy, in the words of the sweep's brief of 2026-10-22, and the coordinator applies it.
  3. October said to replace a pointer to a removed entry "by the skill's file and section in words". That would make a fact cite a skill, which the curator's word of 2026-11-24 forbids ("Facts can never cite skill."). The draft keeps only "drop it where the sentence stands without it", and the worker lists each pointer that it cannot drop. This change is his to confirm.

**New:**

- `briefs/test-copies.txt`: a wrapper with no rule of its own. It hands one worker the kit's README, "How to run it", steps 1 to 5, with the changes of the scenarios folder's README, and the values of the run. It also has the worker copy `questions.md` and `key.md` into the test folder, where the grader's brief looks for them.
- In the script: the order of the stages and its stops; the map returning its chunks and cases as data, through a schema, beside the final message that its brief asks for; the scouts' file in the chunk folder, as the diff's adjustment 15 names it; `map-lines.py`, which adds the map's lines for a chunk's entries to that file, and the Sonnet step that runs it; the pilot's mix run as one chunk named `pilot-1`; the readers writing their answers straight to `answers-X.md` and `answers-Y.md`, by `test.x`, where the kit's step 7 copied them after, with the arms given in the run's result instead of a file.

**Not used:** October's writers' briefs (`05`, `05b`, `06` in `../../evidence/october-briefs/`). The clarity workflow's writer takes their place, since the clarity workflow is the batch mode's way in (`../../WORKFLOW-DIFF.md`, 3.2). The October writers' goal and measure are adjustment 16 of `../../ADJUSTMENTS.md`, a change inside the clarity writer's brief, not here. The two trials of 2026-10-13, `01` on the largest entries and `02` on pairs of FACTS and POSITIONS entries on one ground, made the definition of an entry; the diff counts that step as done once (B2).

**Where October's scout brief and today's differ.** Today's form is `../../evidence/consolidation/scout-brief.md`. The draft keeps October's words. Today's brief also:

- prints each entry and its history by number (`facts-extract.sh 'F-87'`, `'history:F-87'`), and finds the entries that cite it by number (`grep 'F-87\b'`), with the files under `.claude/skills/`. October's finds the earlier texts and the citing entries by the title's opening words;
- gives the commit from the history's first block, where October's gives the first and the last commit by `git log -S` on the title;
- checks each test, file, script and path that the entry names, and whether the entry's words about a ledger row agree with the row's status now ("Exists today");
- greps the worker skill and FACTS for two or three of the entry's key terms, and quotes each place that says the same ("Said elsewhere");
- gives the curator's dated words for any entry, where October's does it for POSITIONS only;
- says to write no opinion on what to cut, to run no build, suite or test, to commit nothing and to launch no agents; its final message lists the entries with something not found or in disagreement, where October's is one line.

## How it was checked

- The harness's parse, as `explorations/coordinator/tools/workflow-scenarios.js` does it: the script's text, with `export const meta` made `const meta`, is accepted as the body of an async function. `node --check` passes. The script holds no backtick and no non-ASCII character, its `meta` is a pure literal, and every `phase()` title is in `meta.phases`.
- A dry run of thirteen ways in, the script run with its hooks stubbed: the agents and the child run that each way in starts, in their order; each launch message names a brief that exists and gives every placeholder of that brief, and only those, with nothing undefined; each map-lines step names the helper and the chunk's entries; the child run gets the clarity script, `out` + `chunks/`, a stream and named chunks. Eleven wrong sets of arguments are refused before any agent starts, each naming what is missing. A claims worker or a map that returns nothing ends the run before the next stage.
- `map-lines.py` run on the pilot's two sets of 2026-11-24 with the map of that night: every entry found in `map.json` and in its claims file, and a second call leaves one section, not two.

## What a first run must prove

Nothing here has run. A first run must show:

1. That the clarity workflow runs as a child of this script. `record-landing.js` starts the orientation workflow that way; no script has started the clarity workflow that way.
2. That the map returns its chunks and its cases through the schema, and that `map.json` and `MAP.md` agree with them.
3. That the clarity workflow holds the map's chunks of 20 to 32 entries. It ran on 10-22 with chunks of 12, and its README says "about ten entries"; `references/record.md` says 20 to 32. If its writer, cold reader or checker cannot hold such a chunk, the map's chunks must be cut smaller with each subject kept in one chunk.
4. That the writer follows the map's lines in `scout.md`: its splits, merges and moved claims inside the chunk, and what it does with a part that the map sends outside the chunk. This is the main thing a first run shows. Without adjustment 15, the assessor and the writer read no `scout.md`, and the map reaches them only through which entries share a chunk.
5. That the checker and the judge pass a claim moved from one entry to another of the chunk, and that the files of a chunk show where each claim went.
6. That October's scout brief, which finds earlier texts and citing entries by the title's words, finds them now that entries cite each other by number.
7. That the claims step works without the morning's scouts' files: on 2026-11-24 its workers copied the checks of the scouts that had run that morning on the record as it stood. In this order the scouts run after the sorting, so `checks` holds only what earlier work wrote.
8. That the claims and map workers can commit and push from inside a Workflow run while other agents commit to `main`; their briefs follow the `fortress-repo` skill's `references/committing.md` for that.
9. The test stage end to end: the copies made by one worker from the kit's steps, a second test after a first (the copies `/home/user/record-test-p` and `-q` may still exist), and the readers' answers written straight under X and Y.
10. The leave and sweep briefs after their changes; the sweep's list of words to delete is that of 2026-10-22.
11. `kind: 'positions'` for the scouts and the clarity runs; the sorting is for FACTS only.

## What waits for the curator's word

- His yes to this draft. At the move to `explorations/coordinator/tools/record-batch/`, the script's constant `HERE` changes to the new folder. The briefs are `.txt` here so that `check-index.sh` does not count them as notes without an INDEX line; under `tools/`, which that check skips, they can take `.md` like the other tools' briefs. `tools/tier-mode.sh` does not switch this script, as it does not switch the clarity workflow's.
- Adjustment 15 of `../../ADJUSTMENTS.md`, without which the clarity assessor and writer read neither the scouts' evidence nor the map's lines ("How the map reaches the writer"). Beyond it, two choices that the first run informs: whether the writer's brief says to follow the map's disposition, and how a claim reaches an entry outside its chunk.
- The Fable grader of the test stage. The kit has a Fable grader. `references/delegating.md`, "Which tier runs what", gives a go in advance to four kinds of Fable work, and the record test's grader is not among them.
- The leave brief's third change, on pointers to a removed entry.
- Which of today's scout items, if any, he wants beside October's.

content.content:
<!-- The brief of the writers of the pilot of the whole record's consolidation (round 1, a mix of cases; round 2, one whole chunk), written by the coordinator on 2026-11-24 from the October writers' brief, the definition of an entry, the clarity writer's rules and the curator's rules of that day; kept in the repository so that the step can be run again. -->

# Brief: a writer of the consolidation's pilot

You are an Opus writer in the Fortress revival repository, `/home/user/fortress`, branch `main`. You rewrite a set of entries of the project's record of facts, `explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md`, as a pilot that the curator, the person in charge, reads before the whole record is consolidated. You run no Fortress program. Load the `fortress-repo` skill (Skill tool) and read its parts `references/records.md` and `references/committing.md`. Keep every wait under 240 s.

## The goal

The curator's words (2026-10-13): "I really hope that the consolidated record is significantly smaller than before. Like that is a goal. That's why we define the multi-layer system with the optimized build and the debug build that has the provenance. So that must pay off. That when the facts and positions get loaded. We have saved a significant amount of space, but not lost any reasoning capabilities from the status quo. We want to have better performance and much lower memory cost. That's the goal."

His words of 2026-11-24, which bound it: "We are not supposed to be cutting for cutting. ... Facts can be larger than 600. That's not a problem on its own. It is a problem when the sum is too large. So if the sources for growth are like duplication and restatement of the same things between facts, that must go. We must use reference pointing." And: "the workers and you as a coordinator have been pre-trained on some knowledge about Fortress, and facts are recording the deviations from your knowledge. Like, this is for in-context learning."

So the record gets small by saying each thing once, under the entry that owns its subject. It does not get small by cutting words out of an entry.

## What you read first

1. The definition of an entry: the `coordinator` skill's `references/record.md` (`/home/user/fortress/.claude/skills/coordinator/references/record.md`), sections "What an entry is" and "A consolidation", and the five worked examples that it names (`explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh 'doc:explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/record-rule-draft.md#Worked examples'`). Follow them exactly. Its six questions decide where a sentence goes. A sentence moves to its home; it is never lost.
2. The October writers' brief, `explorations/coordinator/postmortem-2026-11-24-record-regrowth/evidence/october-briefs/05b-writers-template-after-edit.md` (or the file `05b-*` of that folder): its rules for an entry's line, its provenance line, its pointers and its merges hold for you.
3. The clarity writer's rules for writing an entry: `/home/user/rec-adjust/explorations/coordinator/tools/record-clarity/writer.md`, its section "How to write each entry". Every condition, exception and limit of a claim stays. Clarity comes first. 600 characters is a check, not a cap.
4. The sorting map: `explorations/coordinator/postmortem-2026-11-24-record-regrowth/evidence/sorting-map/MAP.md`, its sections 3 (the subjects and their owners), 4 (the groups of overlap), 5 (each entry's disposition) and 7 (the pilot); `map.json` beside it holds the same as data. For each of your entries, its claims by subject and kind are in the file `claims-<chunk>.md` of that folder that holds the entry (`grep -l` for its number).
5. For each of your entries, what today's checks found: `evidence/stale-claims.md` in the post-mortem folder, and the scout's file that holds the entry, `evidence/consolidation/scout-<chunk>.md` (for entries of the section "The harness and the gate", `pilot/chunk-harness-gate.md`).

## The rules

- **One subject for each entry.** Where the map splits an entry, each part goes to the entry that owns its subject, and the entry keeps the part that its title states. Where no entry owns a subject, write a new entry for it.
- **Merge where one home is right.** Where two entries say the same, one keeps the claim whole and the other points to it, or the two become one entry.
- **A claim leaves an entry only in one of these ways:** it stands whole, with its conditions, in an entry that this one points to; or it goes word for word to the history (the tool does this with the old line), to the report that the entry cites, or to the gap ledger row of its defect. If none of these holds a claim that a reader needs, the claim stays.
- **A defect's description belongs to its ledger row.** The entry keeps the row's number with a few words on what the row holds. Check with `explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh 'ledger:N'` that the row holds what you take out of the entry; if it does not, write the row's new text as a proposal in your report (below), and keep the claim in the entry until then.
- **A fact never cites a skill,** and that a skill says a thing is never a reason to cut it from a fact.
- **A fact does not point back at the decision that it builds.** Leave out a sentence such as "It builds P-45". A pointer to another fact stays.
- **Tests:** where a test guards the fact, the entry names that one test, or one name pattern, not a list. Before another test name leaves, check that the report that the entry cites names it; list those that no report names in your report.
- **History, plans and status leave the entry:** dates, batches, repairs, what is built or still to build. The tool keeps the old line in the history.
- **Detail that is needed only while doing the work** stays in the report, and the entry names the section.
- **A claim that today's checks found false, stale or beyond its support:** reword it to what its support holds, where the finding shows that plainly. Where it does not, keep the claim and list it under "to investigate". Delete no fact silently.
- **Remove no entry** unless the map merges it into another; then say where each of its claims went.
- **Write halfway to ASD-STE100:** plain short sentences, one word for one thing, each term explained where a reader new to the project would need it. Each entry is one line with a bold title that states the fact. A pointer is the other entry's number with a few words on what it holds.
- **Length:** no entry is cut to reach a size. For each entry over 600 characters, name in your report the question of the definition that keeps its extra sentences.

## What you do

1. Make a work tree of your own: `git worktree add /home/user/rec-pilot-@KEY@ HEAD` (detached; create and push no branch). Work only there.
2. Write the apply file for `explorations/coordinator/tools/record.py` (its usage is in its header): each entry that changes, rewritten as one line with its provenance line under it, each new entry, and each merge.
3. In your work tree, run `record.py apply` with your file and then `record.py check --base HEAD`. Fix the file until the check passes. **Change nothing in the main tree's record, and do not commit in your work tree.** Leave the work tree in place with your file applied: the coordinator runs a test on it.
4. Copy your apply file to `/home/user/fortress/explorations/coordinator/postmortem-2026-11-24-record-regrowth/evidence/pilot-2/round-@KEY@.apply`, and write beside it `round-@KEY@.md`, with a header comment that says in one sentence what it is. It holds:
   - for each case or entry, in the map's order: the entry's number; its old text; its new text; and **for each claim that left it, where the claim now stands**: the entry (with the sentence), the history, the report section, or the ledger row. This list is what the curator checks, so no claim may be missing from it;
   - each new entry, with the subject that it owns and the entries that its claims came from;
   - the size of your entries before and after, in characters, each entry and the sum;
   - each entry over 600 characters, with the question that keeps its length;
   - the ledger rows whose text must change so that a defect's description has its home, each as a proposal with the words to add; and the defects that have no row;
   - the test names that no cited report holds;
   - the claims to investigate;
   - each place where the map's disposition was wrong or could not be followed, and what you did.
5. Commit the two files in the main tree, by their paths, with the skill's footer, and push the three refs as the committing part says for work on `main`. The folder is an evidence folder, so it needs no INDEX line. If `git log origin/main..main` shows only your own commits and those of other finished workers of the post-mortem folder, push them together.

Your final message, at most 15 lines: the two files and their commit; the number of entries before and after; the size before and after; what the check showed; the splits, the merges and the new entries, one line each; and what you could not do.
